waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target; high triglycerides alone do not change water needs. Drink more in heat, exercise or fever per general rules. With heart disease, heart failure, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, the app shows only the general range and never pushes a higher target. Choose water, plain chaas and unsweetened drinks; avoid sweet chai, soft drinks, packaged juice, sharbat and alcohol. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose high triglycerides; a blood test reviewed by a doctor is needed.
The app never suggests starting, stopping, skipping or changing any medicine, supplement or dose. Follow your doctor.
Triglycerides of 500 mg/dL or more can cause acute pancreatitis. The app does not set food targets at this level; talk to your doctor. 1000 mg/dL or more needs urgent review.

Omega-3 doses of 2-4 g/day are treatment doses (prescription dose) for the doctor to decide; over-the-counter fish-oil capsules are not a substitute for a prescription (AHA 2019). Prescription omega-3 has a dose-related atrial fibrillation warning (EMA via MHRA).
Some medicines can raise triglycerides (for example thiazide diuretics, beta-blockers, oral estrogen, corticosteroids). Do not stop any medicine; ask your doctor.
Poorly controlled diabetes and an underactive thyroid are common causes of high triglycerides; the doctor checks these first.
Alcohol: best none; none at all if triglycerides are 500 mg/dL or more (NLA 2023).
Emergency: sudden severe upper abdominal pain that spreads to the back, with vomiting; or chest pain or stroke signs. Seek emergency care now.
With heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, follow your doctor's advice on fluids.

requires_doctor_input is true because high triglycerides can reach a pancreatitis-risk level and often have a medical cause or need a prescription; the app sets only general sugar, refined-carbohydrate, alcohol, fibre, saturated-fat, sodium and activity guidance on its own.
